content_of_post_to_comment:
I can’t fall asleep properly. I don’t think it’s insomnia; it just feels like there’s some kind of problem. Usually, I only manage to fall asleep around 3–5 a.m., and then I wake up at around 10:00 a.m.

Additional context:

I am 17 years old. On the first day of trying to fix this, I stayed awake the entire 24-hour day because I thought sleep deprivation would help me crash early. On the second day, I went to bed and actually managed to wake up on my own without an alarm, which gave me hope. But on the third day, the problems immediately returned—I couldn’t fall asleep properly again, and the exact same thing happened on the fourth day.

When I’m lying in bed at night, my mind starts racing, and I just keep tossing and turning for hours. I’ve tried basic things like background sounds and routine adjustments, but my internal clock feels completely stuck on the late-night shift.

My goal: I want to be able to go to sleep normally (at a reasonable hour) and wake up by myself around 9–10 a.m. without an alarm, keeping a healthy rhythm.

Could you give me some advice? What should I do to fix this loop, how can I actually fall asleep without spending hours staring at the ceiling, and what daily habits or routines should I follow during the day to keep my sleep schedule stable?
